title: High-chloride hyperpolarization suppresses KRAS tumors, so the effect is ion-independent

fields.label: Label
fields.value: High-chloride hyperpolarization suppresses KRAS tumors, so the effect is ion-independent

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Raising extracellular chloride, which hyperpolarizes cells through native chloride channels, decreases the incidence of KRASG12D-induced tumor-like structures in Xenopus laevis embryos by about 38%, showing that tumor suppression depends on the change in membrane voltage rather than on the Kv1.5 channel or on potassium specifically.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Long-range hyperpolarization suppresses the formation of ITLS

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Treatment with high chloride (whose uptake by native Cl− channels hyperpolarizes cells) resulted in a 37.5% decrease (N=349; t-test P<0.05) in KRASG12D ITLS, demonstrating that the suppressive effect is not specific for Kv1.5 nor for potassium, as mediators of the crucial Vmem change (Fig. 2C).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Chernet BT, Levin M, “Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range”, Oncotarget (2014), doi:10.18632/oncotarget.1935; section “RESULTS › Long-range hyperpolarization suppresses the formation of ITLS”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryos injected with KRASG12D mRNA and raised in elevated (70 mM) chloride medium

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2014-tumor-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The alternative ionic manipulation is informative and the reported incidence is testable from published measurements. It weakens channel-specific explanations but does not cleanly prove that voltage alone mediates suppression.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare KRAS-induced tumor incidence under high chloride and normal medium while directly confirming hyperpolarization, then compare with potassium-channel intervention. Similar suppression by distinct ionic routes supports a voltage-mediated effect.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The existing study does not fully isolate ion-independent downstream pathways.

Raw records are not clearly deposited.

High chloride has physiological effects beyond Vmem.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.95
discriminating power: 0.6
data existence: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The chloride contrast is a published numerical result aimed at separating voltage from the Kv1.5 protein. The percentage and sample size can be inspected directly. Osmotic and ionic confounds, and the lack of raw voltage traces, keep the ion-independence conclusion from being fully resolvable on the published summary.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare KRASG12D tumor-like-structure incidence in normal medium and in 70 mM chloride, with membrane voltage measured through native chloride conductance and with Kv1.5 absent. A reduction near the reported 38% that tracks hyperpolarization would support ion-independent voltage dependence; no change, or a change without hyperpolarization, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
High external chloride also changes osmolarity and chloride chemical driving force.

Animal-level voltages and incidence records are not deposited.
